newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends sharply up on heavy LME gain.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends sharply up on heavy LME gain.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply up in active trading on Friday due to heavy overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at 21,260 yuan ($2,562) per tonne, rising 480 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 20,780 and hit a high of 21,290.
January rose 230 to 20,550, February 270 to 20,720, March 420 to 21,030, May 460 to 21,260 and June 510 to 21,300.
Combined volume rose sharply to 133,210 tonnes from 17,220.
Copper opened higher and rose further before most contracts closing near their intra-day highs.
Traders said LME gains boosted the confidence of long position holders and large amounts of speculative money surged into market.
"Stop-loss buying triggered more follow-up speculative buying, which made copper breach the key 21,000 yuan resistance level easily," one trader said.
"Market sentiment improved a lot with many investors expecting copper to rise above 21,500 yuan in the next few days, unless LME stockpiles rise sharply," he added.
The stockpile data on the LME will be announced tonight.
But some traders said open interest fell sharply today, indicating many investors had liquidated their long positions at high levels.
"Large amounts of long liquidation suggested some investors do not think copper will see any further sharp rises," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended up with the only traded January 1997 contract rising 140 yuan to end at 13,960 yuan per tonne on volume of 710 tonnes.
